brief: A calendar showing energy levels — mornings are high ground, post-lunch dips are valleys

dominant_strengths: Earthy peak-to-valley palette feels narratively appropriate, encoding circadian energy as terrain rather than abstract numeric heatmap.
Bar-chart-in-cell metaphor is inventive — each day reads as a small ridgeline you can scan at a glance.
Typography hierarchy is clean: oversized title, restrained day numbers, faded out-of-month days correctly recede.
dominant_weaknesses: Five identical-shape ridgelines per day make patterns indistinguishable; the brief's morning-peak / post-lunch-valley story isn't legible without a legend decode.
X-axis of each mini-chart lacks time labels (AM/noon/PM), so 'valley' position carries no temporal meaning to the eye.
Selected state (Nov 14) uses a flat yellow wash that clashes with the muted cream/sage system and feels like a default highlight, not crafted.
fix_priorities: Add subtle time-of-day axis ticks or AM/PM anchors beneath bars so valleys read as post-lunch, not arbitrary.
Differentiate days more — vary bar heights meaningfully or aggregate into a single sparkline per cell to avoid repetitive sameness.
Refine selection treatment: thin border or warm sand tint instead of saturated yellow block.
Introduce hover/expand interaction so a clicked day reveals the actual hourly curve.
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept is strong and visceral palette is pleasant, but behavioral legibility lags because the repeating five-bar motif resists quick scanning.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually on-brief — it does encode energy as terrain — but the chosen chart form undersells the morning-peak / afternoon-valley narrative the brief promises.
